app.title: ChemoSuite: multi-instrument spectra to fused descriptors and a sample-class model
app.summary: A person picks one analytical module at a time from a sidebar. Each module brings in that instrument's files (peak lists, fluorescence matrices, IR, NMR, thermal, chromatography or elemental tables), or a folder, a ZIP batch or a synthetic benchmark. In each module they clean and calibrate the signals, compute descriptors per sample (for example molecular formulas or decomposition components) and send the descriptor table to a shared session. In the fusion module they join every block by sample ID, type a class label for each sample and fit a discriminant model. They then judge it from its fit metrics, its scores plot with a confidence ellipse, a permutation test and the variable-importance ranking, and export a multi-sheet report, the fused matrix and the ranked markers, or save the whole session as a project file.

task.text: Turn raw instrument outputs from several analytical techniques into per-sample descriptors, fuse them, and fit and validate a model that separates sample classes and ranks the descriptors that drive the separation.

data.text: Instrument signals for a set of samples, one file per sample and technique (mass peak lists, excitation-emission matrices, IR/NMR spectra, thermal curves, chromatograms, elemental tables). These become descriptor tables with one row per sample, joined by sample ID into a single feature matrix with a class column.
data.item: a sample measured by one or more analytical techniques, carried as one row of descriptors

stage.text: processing instrument spectra into descriptors and classifying samples, after measurement and before reporting

mechanism.text: A sidebar module picker switches between per-technique studios. Each studio has a sidebar file manager driving tabbed plots and tables for the active sample and pushes its descriptor table into shared session state. The fusion studio assembles those tables into an editable matrix, fits the chosen model, and shows metrics, scores, importance and validation in tabs with download buttons.

field.text: multi-technique spectroscopy with chemometric data fusion and PLS-DA classification in analytical chemistry

workflow.name: turn several measurement types per sample into one feature table and fit a class model

steps.here: choose a technique module in the sidebar, then upload files, scan a local folder, upload a ZIP batch or load a synthetic benchmark; a saved .chemo project can restore everything

pick m/z and intensity columns, crop the m/z range, set a noise cutoff and normalisation; correct mass drift with a polynomial fitted to matched calibrant peaks (order dropped to linear when calibrants span too little of the range)

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: assign molecular formulas within ppm tolerance and element bounds with an optional 13C isotope check; fit PARAFAC to fluorescence matrices; compute indices per sample and send the descriptor table to the fusion module

steps.step: join the tables by sample and label each sample's class
steps.here: assemble every session block (or uploaded descriptor CSVs, or a batch screen) by Sample_ID into one matrix; only the Class_Target column is editable, pre-filled from sample names

steps.step: fit a model and check that it holds
steps.here: choose PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, sparse PLS-DA or multiblock variants, low- or mid-level fusion, latent variables, block scaling and permutation count; read R2X/R2Y/Q2/accuracy, a 2D/3D scores plot with a Hotelling ellipse, VIP ranking, S-plot and permutation p-value
download a multi-sheet Excel or HTML passport, the fused matrix CSV and the ranked biomarker CSV, or save the session as a .chemo project

distinctive: each technique is its own studio that publishes a per-sample descriptor block into a shared session, so fusion depends on samples sharing an ID across instruments
blocks are scaled by 1/sqrt(number of variables) so a technique with many descriptors does not swamp one with few
a warning appears when descriptors outnumber samples and there are fewer than 20 samples, because the class separation may be over-optimistic
mass-scale recalibration falls back to a linear fit when the matched calibrants cover less than 60% of the mass range
variable importance is coloured by the technique each descriptor came from, so the person sees which instrument drives the separation
